about: Every vault behind this site: what each holds, who writes to it, and how to open it. Three kinds of credential appear here. A vault key reads and writes; it is never published. A read key reads only and cannot be turned into a vault key; the two public vaults publish theirs. An append token adds rows to one lane and cannot read anything; the telemetry lane publishes its token so every page can write to it.

vaults.name: The evidence vault
vaults.holds: The story as it was assembled on the morning of 22 October 2026: every source as a folder with its capture (text, screenshot, HTML, headers, sha256 of each), the claims and the dated events each agent extracted, the editor's memos and the agents' notes. Its own app explores them.
vaults.writers: the collectors, the story-site agent and the newsroom lead; the editor

vaults.name: The source watch
vaults.holds: Every outside source on the story, watched on a schedule: country, sector, publisher and page; what access each check had; a snapshot whenever the content changed; and every snapshot and every change as a graph. A pack-mode vault (sgit-ai 0.24.0 or later): it clones and pushes in seconds.
vaults.facts: a pack-mode vault; sgit-ai 0.24.0 or later reads it
vaults.writers: researcher@php.newsroom, the agent that runs the watch
vaults.note: No read key is published yet: pack vaults do not open in the vault UI, and the key will be published with that support.

vaults.name: The telemetry vault
vaults.access: private, with a public append lane
vaults.holds: One anonymous event per page view (page, referrer host, country, region and city; no IP address, no cookie), each encrypted in the reader's browser to a key held by the drainer, and the counts drained from them.
vaults.writers: every page of this site, through the write-only lane; dev@php.newsroom drains it
vaults.facts: imports the telemetry application (5wnsr5h8) at telemetry-ux/, read-only; opened with its vault key and the server access token, its Queue & drain page drains the lane in the browser
vaults.note: It opens as its own dashboard: the application is not in it but in a vault of its own, versioned there, which this vault links inside itself and loads on open. The key that decrypts the events sits in it sealed under a passphrase (identity/drain-key.json); the passphrase is typed by whoever drains.

vaults.name: The public telemetry stats
vaults.holds: The curated, public view of the telemetry: page views and sessions per hour and per day for readers, for the editor, team and power users, for synthetic visitors and for crawlers; and, over readers only, countries (with a world map), devices, languages, site versions, pages and referrer hosts. Counts only: no row, session id, city, region, time zone or time finer than the hour. Written at every drain.
vaults.facts: written by admin/build/telemetry_publish.py from the telemetry vault (84wr8mib) at every drain; its own app

vaults.name: The subscriptions vault
vaults.access: private, with a public append lane
vaults.holds: Subscription requests (an email address, what to follow, how often), each encrypted in the reader's browser to a key held by the editor and the agent that sends, and the list of addresses with their status: requested, confirmed or left.
vaults.writers: readers, through the write-only lane on /subscribe/; dev@php.newsroom drains it; the agent at agent@diniscruz.ai confirms and sends

vaults.name: The coverage vault
vaults.holds: How other outlets presented the story: 24 pages (the BBC live page, CNN, The Register, The Hacker News, php.net, CISA, NCSC-NL, Wiz, Calif, php2shell.com, the PHPocalypse Tracker and more) captured on 22 October 2026 between 17:20 and 17:45 UTC, each with desktop, full-page and phone screenshots, the page text and a provenance file with the SHA-256 of every file; and the review of what this site should learn from them. Third-party pages, kept for the record and never republished.
vaults.writers: claude-story-site, the agent that designs this site
vaults.note: The review written from it is published in the repository; its findings become facts on this site only once they cite a capture.

vaults.name: The conductor vault
vaults.holds: Where the team is: the roster, the plan that opens every run and the digest that closes it, the broadcasts, and what members send the conductor through its lane, one token per member, each message encrypted to the conductor's key.
vaults.writers: conductor@php.newsroom only; every member of the team reads it
vaults.note: Its read key goes to members privately; the lane's tokens are not published.

vaults.name: The issues vault
vaults.holds: The team's tasks as files (Issues-FS-lite): one queue per member with open, blocked and done, one markdown card per task. The board on this site is a snapshot of it.
vaults.writers: each member of the team, only inside its own queue
vaults.note: Its key goes to members privately.

vaults.name: The mail vault
vaults.holds: The team's messages (Email-FS-lite): a mailroom, an inbox, a done folder and an outbox per member, and each member's session notes.
vaults.writers: each member of the team, in its own folders and other members' mailrooms
vaults.note: Its key goes to members privately.

vaults.name: The telemetry application
vaults.holds: The application that reads the telemetry, and nothing else: eight pages (overview, audience, content, journeys, sources and devices, every event, the lane's queue and its drain, about), versioned in the vault itself: a VERSION file, a changelog and one commit per release. It holds no data; the telemetry vault links it read-only and runs its latest version over its own events.
vaults.facts: linked read-only inside the telemetry vault (84wr8mib) at telemetry-ux/; v0.1.1
vaults.note: It is held by the editor, sealed to the editor's key on pki.sgit.ai. Nothing in it is secret.

vaults.name: The telemetry dashboard (superseded)
vaults.holds: A vault app that draws the telemetry: page views by hour, pages, countries, regions and cities, devices, referrers, languages, versions, pages per session and the latest events, each a filter. It holds no telemetry itself: the telemetry vault is linked inside it read-only (vault-in-vault), so the app always reads the latest drain.
vaults.facts: links the telemetry vault (84wr8mib) at telemetry/, read-only
vaults.note: Superseded on 22 October by the telemetry application (5wnsr5h8), which the telemetry vault now imports: the data vault opens the app, not the other way round. It is held by the editor, sealed to the editor's key on pki.sgit.ai. Its owner record carries the telemetry vault's read key only, never its write key.

vaults.name: The collaborators vault
vaults.access: private, with a public append lane
vaults.holds: What the collaborators send from /collaborators/: requests to join (a name, an email address, the reader closest to them) and feedback on each ask, each encrypted in the sender's browser to a key held by the conductor and the editor.
vaults.writers: collaborators and anyone else, through the write-only lane on /collaborators/; conductor@php.newsroom drains it; the editor reads it
vaults.note: Its key, the lane's enum key and the key pair's passphrase are never published.

vaults.name: The schedule vault (retired)
vaults.holds: Retired on 24 October 2026, kept as an archive: the first schedules, tasks and runs. Schedules, runs and messages are now kept in the site's repository (/team/schedule/).

vaults.name: The synthetic board member's vault
vaults.holds: Every run of the synthetic board member against this site: for each page it read, the served and the rendered HTML, the text, the first screen and the full page as images and the measurements; every request with its status, size, timing and sha256; every console message; what the reviewer was given and the review it wrote.
vaults.note: Its read key is published at the editor's request (24 October 2026): it holds nothing confidential, only captures of this public site and the reader's reviews.
